why: The report provides school-level evidence that coherent alignment of people, policies, programs, culture, and family engagement—not merely installing isolated structures—supports instructional improvement.

This is a study-specific design and implementation of a named social-robot chassis for particular learners, rather than a general instructional element; its construction activity is only an instance of Hands-on Learning or Makerspace use.
RSAV is a task-specific computational model fitted to probabilistic reversal-learning data, not a general learning theory, and its claims are empirical findings about model fit and age differences.
RSAT is a named computer-based reading-comprehension and strategy-use assessment instrument rather than a reusable instructional element.
name: RSAT
product_description: RSAT is a computer-based online assessment developed by Gonny Schellings and colleagues to measure readers’ comprehension and spontaneous reading-strategy use during sentence-by-sentence reading.

why: This is a literature-review taxonomy of inconsistently defined relationships-and-sexuality-education terms, not a general explanatory theory of learning or a method for studying learning.
This is a review-derived taxonomy for classifying and reporting pedagogical approaches in school-based relationships and sexuality education, not a general theory of learning or teaching.
name: Taxonomy of teaching approaches used to deliver school-based RSE

why: The RSIPAS is a named self-report measurement instrument rather than a general instructional element.
name: Religious/Spiritually Integrated Practice Assessment Scale (RSIPAS)
product_description: The RSIPAS is a 40-item validated self-report scale developed by Oxhandler and colleagues to measure nurses' competencies in integrating clients' religion and spirituality into clinical practice.
